meta.title: Week 47 at OpenAEC: everything that is new | OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: 17 GitHub accounts, 27 projects, 1,366 improvements and 96 resolved issues: OpenAEC's weekly roundup, by project and with screenshots.

article.t002: 17 GitHub accounts worked on 27 projects and made 1,366 improvements. Here is everything that happened.
article.t014: First drawing delivered with our own BIM modeller
article.t015: We are building two competing BIM modellers: the Modeller in Open BIM Suite and Open BIM Studio. Neither is ready for production yet.
article.t017: OpenAEC now has its own forum, with sign-in and an account menu at the top right of the site.
article.t019: The OpenAEC Academy offers courses on construction drawings and Open FEM Studio.
article.t021: Open BIM Validator is available with its own Windows installer.
article.t023: All Open BIM Suite modules, features, formats and downloads on one page.
article.t025: 765 subscribers and 11 videos on the channel.
article.t029: Follow progress and new features on Instagram.
article.t031: Follow the OpenAEC Foundation on LinkedIn.
article.t034: SuperCloud brings Frappe, a CDE, document management and IFCX together in one environment for the entire construction project. The product is in development: currently with 6 major customers, opening worldwide on 1 January.
article.t035: This week: 47 improvements to infrastructure and deployment.

article.t145: How we counted: public repositories of the OpenAEC Foundation, commits on the main branch from Monday 16 November through Saturday 21 November 2026. Merges, bots and automated data updates are excluded. Line counts cover all changed files, including tests and documentation. One person may use multiple GitHub accounts. Screenshots of Suite, Geotechniek, Planner, Pile Plan, Frame, Calc and IFCX were taken on 21 November in the live web versions; those of the other tools and SuperCloud come from earlier captures. The real-world project has been anonymised: customer, location and coordinates have been removed. SuperCloud improvements are in private repositories and are excluded from the totals. The 133 Open Office Studio improvements are also excluded because they are still on working branches.
